mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS remains above 5.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained unemployment above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during triggered manufacturing contraction episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4% signals a stagflation risk, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% AND CPIAUCSL > 4% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods of simultaneous high FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as earnings growth expectations rise.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of rapid payroll growth acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rebound in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) above their prior six-month averages signals a recovery in aggregate demand, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 6mo moving average AND HOUST > 6mo moving average in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of coordinated GDPC1 and HOUST rebounds above six-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals an expansion in manufacturing activity, which improves corporate revenue prospects and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during periods of sustained INDPRO expansion above its 12-month moving average.
